newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean ports not affected by strikes - officials.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean ports not affected by strikes - officials.

text.p: South Korea's two biggest ports were operating normally on Tuesday despite an all-out strike call by the country's biggest union body, port officials said.
"All port operations are normal. I don't see any sign of disruption in the port," said Yoon Kyong-cho, an official in charge of shipment at Pusan, South Korea's largest port.
A spokeman at the port of Inchon, the country's second largest, said: "Congestion is not any worse than usual. Everything is normal and there's no stoppage."

The Federation of Korean Trade Unions with 1.2 million members has called for a two-day strike from Tuesday to protest against a controversial new labour law that allows employers to dismiss workers and replace strikers.
The federation earlier said it did not want to paralyse port operations but had asked port workers to stage a "partial strike" on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Its call for a public-sector strike had only a limited impact on Tuesday, with subways and buses working normally.
The outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions has said its 500,000 members would join the strike on Wednesday.
